data.name: Usha
data.gender_notes: Usha is used as a female name in hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Sanskrit uṣas, 'dawn', from the root vas, 'to shine'. Its root is Sanskrit uṣas (उषस्). Usha, the Vedic goddess of dawn. Usha is a Sanskrit name meaning “Dawn; the goddess of dawn”. Families who choose it generally do so for the quality the name expresses.
data.spiritual_meaning: Usha expresses “Dawn; the goddess of dawn”; spiritual readings of the name are interpretive.
data.etymology: From the Sanskrit uṣas, 'dawn', from the root vas, 'to shine'.
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Usha total 13, reducing to 4. Number 4 is associated with discipline, order and steady effort.

vedic_reference.note: Goddess Usha, daughter of Surya, the sun god, and Sanjana, is the goddess of dawn. She is also known as Samudra Vasini, the goddess of the sea, and is often depicted riding on a chariot drawn by seven horses.
